classification_accuracy: Classifiers on the same 1,000 development messages; whiskers are marginal 95% Wilson accuracy intervals. The three supervised classifiers used 5,992 labeled fitting examples; LLM classifiers used zero-shot intent names. These are different task-specific training conditions.
llm_confidence: Within each Claude model, the original, verifier and learned scores retain identical selected labels. Whiskers are conditional 95% bootstrap intervals from 5,000 shared resamples. Learned scores combine extra same-model calls and supervised TF-IDF evidence; no feature ablation identifies the responsible ingredient.
risk_coverage: Descriptive risk–coverage curves on development data; tied scores enter together. The 1% line marks observed risk, while threshold selection uses the upper endpoint of a Wilson interval. The highlighted operating point was selected on these outcomes and requires independent validation.
calibration_mappings: Scalar mappings fitted only on the 1,000 calibration examples. Logistic on score and on log-odds learn slope and intercept with C=1. Isotonic fits a non-decreasing map with clipped out-of-range inputs. Temperature cannot be drawn as one universal map of top confidence because it transforms the full class distribution.
calibration_reliability: The fitted calibration methods evaluated on 1,000 separate development examples. Marker size grows with bin count; thin whiskers are nominal pointwise 95% Wilson intervals. Sparse bins remain uncertain. All methods within a panel retain identical selected labels.
probability_reliability: Reliability comparisons on the same 1,000 development examples. Each row holds the classifier's selected labels fixed. Points show mean reported correctness probability versus observed fraction correct in ten shared equal-width bins; whiskers are nominal 95% Wilson intervals, without multiple-bin adjustment. The diagonal indicates perfect calibration. Count bars below each panel use a logarithmic axis and show every nonempty bin's sample size. Empty bins are omitted; no smoothing or connecting lines are used. OpenAI temperature inputs are log returned probabilities, not native logits. All three Claude models’ learned scores include extra inference calls and supervised TF-IDF evidence.
probability_outcomes: Scores split by observed outcome on the development set. Each curve is normalized within correct or incorrect cases, so its bin shares sum to 100%; the two outcome curves do not show the overall error prevalence. Legend counts retain that denominator. Strong separation helps triage errors, while reliability must be assessed in the other figure. Cross-classifier comparisons involve different mistakes and error rates; comparisons within each Claude model hold the predictions fixed.
reliability_counts: Temperature-scaled embedding LR. Points are equal-width bin averages with 95% Wilson intervals and example counts; empty bins are omitted. No connecting line or smoothing is used. The right panel uses a logarithmic count axis to show both sparse bins and the 899-example final bin.
cost_pareto: Empirical Pareto frontiers on the same 1,000 development examples. Costs are recorded API fees for the calls each pipeline requires, including Claude batch discounts; local compute and fitting costs are excluded. Rings mark non-dominated points and connecting lines are visual guides, not available mixtures. Small Brier differences may be sampling noise. The API-fee-only comparison including local models is intentionally separate from the hosted-only comparisons.
cost_sensitivity: Illustrative sensitivity of the accuracy frontier to the embedding pipeline’s all-in cost per 1,000 future messages. This local cost includes any amortized setup and local inference cost supplied by the decision maker. The four scenario prices are assumptions, not measured PC costs; hosted prices retain the observed batch fees and exclude their own unpriced overhead. Rings indicate empirical non-dominated choices at each assumed cost.
opus_calibration_mappings: Opus native and learned correctness mappings fitted only on the 1,000 calibration outcomes, using the same logistic and isotonic definitions as the earlier classifiers.
opus_calibration_reliability: Opus calibration methods evaluated on the separate 1,000 development outcomes. Marker size reflects bin count; thin whiskers are nominal 95% Wilson intervals. Selected labels remain fixed within each panel.
opus_probability_reliability: Opus original and learned scores on the same 1,000 development messages, with selected labels held fixed. Points use ten shared equal-width bins, with nominal 95% Wilson intervals; count histograms show the evidence in each bin. Empty bins are omitted.
opus_probability_outcomes: Opus confidence distributions normalized separately within correct and incorrect development outcomes. Legend counts give the denominators. Separation measures review-ranking potential, while reliability must be assessed in the companion figure.
